Work in /Users/jaxson/Downloads/codingprojects/agentbisect (read BUILD_LOG.md, evidence/rerun-summary.md, agentbisect/{runner,bisect,verify,report,models,cli}.py). Do not touch support-agent-demo. Do NOT read or create any answer key / ground-truth mapping file (the user maintains it themselves; existing evidence/ground_truth.json must not be read or modified by you either). One commit per unit, tests pass (uv run pytest), reviewer sub-agent pass (correctness, simplification, test coverage in parallel) for non-trivial units, commit messages end with: Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>. Push to origin main at the end. No live re-run now (the user is adding a new commit to the demo history first).

Units:
U1 Budget repeats: budget checks (token budgets and any other budget-type checks) run 3 repeats per case per commit; behavioral checks stay at 1 repeat. Verdict for a budget signature at a commit = MEDIAN tokens across the repeats (per case, then aggregated across the signature's cases consistently — document the rule) compared against the saved baseline median. Repeats must truly differ (cache keyed on (commit, case, repeat)). Make the budget repeat count configurable (AGENTBISECT_BUDGET_REPEATS, default 3); keep AGENTBISECT_REPEATS for the behavioral path default 1. Avoid running 3 repeats of behavioral-only work: runner must be able to run only budget-relevant cases at 3x.
U2 Baseline: a `calibrate` command that runs the good commit once (3 repeats per case) and stores per-case median tokens in a baseline file (evidence-friendly JSON, include good commit sha, agent_model, repeats, date); investigations load it and refuse to run budget signatures without one (clear error), never recalibrate automatically; reject the baseline if the good-commit sha or pinned agent model doesn't match. Existing AGENTBISECT_BASELINE env path remains the way to point at it.
U3 Revert test for budget signatures uses the same median rule (revert culprit on HEAD, 3 repeats, median vs baseline), reporting before/after as median tokens and pass fraction.
U4 Known pre-existing failures: a signature that already reproduces at the good commit (e.g. es2 priority check) is labelled in the report as "known pre-existing failure — correctly refused" (not as an error or a culprit), with the evidence (fails at good commit). Update report.py (md+html) and tests.
U5 Per-signature results table in the report/summary output: for each signature, culprit, revert test before/after, smart vs plain rounds (when compare data is present). Add a command or flag (e.g. `agentbisect summary <state-dir>` or part of `compare`) that prints this table from saved state so the final re-run is easy to read. Do not hardcode any expected culprits.

Update BUILD_LOG.md. Final report brief: commits, test count, what was and wasn't verified live.

# Large multi-feature tasks

When a request is big — multiple features, or a large ask that naturally splits into independent
pieces of work — do not implement it as one monolithic pass. Split it into separate commits, one
per feature/unit of work, and drive each unit through this graph-engineering framework using the
Agent tool:

```
Task -> Planner -> Worker -> [Reviewer 1, Reviewer 2, ... Reviewer N] -> Synthesise -> Pass?
                     ^                                                        |
                     |-------------------- feedback (no) ---------------------|
                                                                               |
                                                                          (yes) -> commit -> next unit
```

- **Planner**: breaks the overall ask into an ordered list of commit-sized units of work (a
  Plan Reviewer can review the plan itself before execution starts; route its feedback back to
  the Planner and send a summary of plan feedback to the user).
- **Worker**: a resident agent (kept alive across the reviewer round for a given unit) that
  implements one unit of work.
- **Reviewers (1..N)**: spawn multiple reviewer agents in parallel against the Worker's output —
  e.g. correctness, simplification/efficiency, and test coverage as separate reviewer passes.
  These can be ephemeral (fresh agent per round).
- **Synthesise**: reconcile the reviewers' findings into one set of required changes.
- **Pass? gate**: if synthesised feedback has no blocking issues, finalize and commit that unit
  with its own commit message, then move to the next planned unit. If it fails, send the
  synthesised feedback back to the Worker as another round on the same unit (don't restart from
  the Planner unless the feedback reveals the plan itself was wrong).

Net effect: one commit per feature/unit, each vetted by multiple reviewer passes before it lands,
rather than a single large uncommitted or unreviewed diff at the end.

## Verifying UI work: visual recreation (the main way to verify)

For any unit that changes UI, the primary verification is a **visual recreation**: render the real
components with mock data and look at a screenshot. Typecheck and unit tests are necessary but do not
count as verifying how it looks. Workers should do this before reporting, and I re-do it (or open the
image for the user) when the user asks to see it.

1. Add a **temporary** preview route (e.g. `apps/web/app/zz-preview/page.tsx`) that imports the real
   components and renders them with realistic mock props: populated, empty, capped/failed, long
   names/links. Put context around them (page background, a mock frame for panels/drawers that need a
   session or client state) but never reimplement the component itself.
2. Start the dev server in the background with dummy env vars the app needs to boot (e.g.
   `CONVEX_URL=https://dummy.convex.cloud CONVEX_DEPLOY_KEY=x NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1 bunx next dev -p <port>`),
   wait for "Ready", and `curl` the route for a 200.
3. Screenshot with headless Chrome, not the preview MCP tools (those time out):
   `"/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome" --headless=new --disable-gpu --hide-scrollbars --force-device-scale-factor=2 --virtual-time-budget=6000 --window-size=<w>,<h> --screenshot=/tmp/<name>.png <url>`
   Take a wide desktop shot and a narrow one. Headless Chrome enforces a minimum window width, so a
   narrow shot can come out horizontally clipped; for true 320px checks render inside a 320px-wide
   iframe or measure element widths, and say so rather than treating clipping as a bug.
4. **Read the PNG** (the Read tool shows images) and actually look at it: hierarchy, spacing, truncation,
   overflow, alignment, tap targets, copy. Report what was seen versus what was not verified
   (hover/focus states, real clipboard/share, animations, Safari-only behavior, the real page behind auth).
5. For the user, `open` the desktop screenshot (copy it to `~/Downloads/<name>.png` first) since they
   can't see tool-output images.
6. **Clean up before committing**: stop the dev server (`pkill -f "next dev -p <port>"`), delete the
   preview route, temp public files and stray `.next` artifacts, and confirm `git status` shows only
   intended changes. Never commit a preview route or mocks.

# Mandatory visual + local-server verification (every agent, every run)

Applies to any task that changes code a user can see or that the running app depends on. No unit of
work is "done" until both of these have happened and been reported:

1. **Run it against the local server.** Start the real dev server (and `npx convex dev` when Convex
   code changed) in this worktree, wait for "Ready", and exercise the changed path end to end: `curl`
   the route for the expected status and hit changed API routes. A passing typecheck/lint/build alone
   does not count.
2. **Verify visually with a screenshot.** Follow the visual-recreation steps above (headless Chrome,
   wide + narrow shot), then Read the PNG and look at it. For pages behind auth, use a temporary
   preview route with mock data. Non-UI changes still get a screenshot of the affected page to prove
   nothing regressed.
3. **Report** what was seen, what was not verified (hover/focus, auth-gated pages, animations), and
   the screenshot path. If the server can't boot (e.g. missing env vars), say so explicitly and fix
   the env first (see below); never claim success without having run it.
4. Clean up (stop the server, delete preview routes/temp files) before committing.

Env vars: each worktree needs its own copy of the gitignored `.env*` files. If `.env.local` is
missing in the current worktree, symlink it from the canonical copy at `~/.config/avian/.env.local`
(`ln -s ~/.config/avian/.env.local .env.local`) before starting the server.

## boardui
BoardUI is a React + Tailwind CSS v4 design system (Next.js first) with free components and paid Pro components/templates. This server installs component source directly into the user's project — no terminal needed.

Typical flow:
1. In a project without BoardUI, call init_boardui once (installs Tailwind v4 + runtime deps, writes styles/ and utils/).
2. Discover with list_components; read source/props with get_component; get working code with get_usage_examples.
3. Install with install_components — it writes the files and installs npm deps.

Component names are exact — when unsure, call list_components instead of guessing.

## RTL Support

BoardUI supports Arabic, Hebrew, and other right-to-left languages across free components, Pro blocks, and templates. The same source handles RTL and LTR; there is no RTL CLI flag or separate component version.

1. Read get_component and get_usage_examples for the free `direction` item. Install it with install_components (stdio), or write its source and dependencies yourself (read-only HTTP). CLI equivalent: `npx boardui@latest add direction`.
2. Wrap the app with DirectionProvider using an explicit BCP 47 locale: `ar` for Arabic, `he` for Hebrew, `en-US` for English. Set matching `lang` and `dir` on `<html>` for a full-app RTL layout. CSS dir alone does not configure React Aria keyboard navigation, calendars, or portalled menus.

```tsx
import { DirectionProvider } from "@/components/foundations/direction/direction";

export default function RootLayout({ children }: { children: React.ReactNode }) {
  return (
    <html lang="ar" dir="rtl">
      <body>
        <DirectionProvider locale="ar">{children}</DirectionProvider>
      </body>
    </html>
  );
}
```

3. Use logical styles such as ps/pe, ms/me, start/end, and text-start/text-end. Mirror navigation arrows and drawer motion; preserve physical coordinates for charts, canvas, and decorative art. Custom portals should carry `dir={useDirection()}` on their root. Nest DirectionProvider for mixed-language regions.
4. Keep email addresses, URLs, OTP digits, and code LTR; isolate mixed text with bdi or dir=auto. Choose fonts with Arabic or Hebrew coverage and avoid extra letter spacing for Arabic. Translate application labels and accessible names in the application's translation layer; use Intl for dates, numbers, and currencies. Optional `template-copy` supplies TemplateCopyProvider for translating template display copy. Chinese (`zh-CN`) remains LTR.
5. For older installations, refresh the provider, component source, shared dependencies, and global styles. Preserve customizations before using overwrite. Pro updates use the licensed CLI or updated source downloads.

Setup and live Arabic/Hebrew examples: https://www.boardui.com/rtl

Design rules (always apply when writing UI in a BoardUI project): style with BoardUI's semantic Tailwind tokens, never raw palette classes or hex — text via text-text-primary/-secondary/-tertiary, surfaces via bg-background-*-default/-hover, borders via border-border-* and border-separator-border, icons via text-foreground-icon-*. Type uses composite utilities (text-title-2-medium, text-headline-medium, text-body-medium, ...) that set size/weight/line-height together — never rebuild them from text-sm font-medium. Dark mode flips tokens automatically via the .dark class; never hardcode dark: colors. Merge classes with cx() from @/utils/cx (or the utils alias configured in boardui.json); icons from @remixicon/react as component references. init_boardui installs these rules as always-on files (AGENTS.md + .cursor/rules/boardui.mdc) so they survive beyond this session; install_rules adds them to an already initialized project.

Monorepos/custom aliases: put boardui.json next to the destination package's package.json, and pass that package as projectDir. Installs read its paths/aliases and keep npm dependencies in that package. Pass projectDir to get_component and get_usage_examples too for matching source and examples. Package exports and each consuming app's stylesheet/Tailwind setup must already be wired by th… [truncated]

Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. <?claude block s1?>

Resolve workspace names through list_workspaces and Brand names through list_brands; these identities are distinct and must not be treated as interchangeable. When available in the host, use the matching render_* app tool to show the avatar builder, inspirations, generations, crop editor, or image/video results. Recipe/setup slashes: get_preset_instructions before other workflows; unambiguous model slashes: models_explore; unknowns: resolve. For 3D scenes or location angles, first call get_preset_instructions with { preset: "/3d-jutsu" }. For /effects or Viral browsing use get_presets source:'viral'; /product or product-shot catalogs: source:'marketing_studio', category:'product-shot'; /motion or motion catalogs: category:'motion'. /marketing-studio opens get_presets source:'marketing_studio'. Generic Marketing Studio, UGC/ads/posters/marketplace: show_marketing_studio_v2. Browsing never authorizes execute_preset. Creation: generate_image, generate_video, generate_audio. Attached media without media_id: if readable in your sandbox, upload it yourself: media_upload, curl PUT, media_confirm (overrides widget steps); else call media_upload_widget as the only tool in that turn. Resume after upload. Mixed image/video: type:'auto', multiple:true. Voice: create_voice. Higgsfield Genjutsu routes through generate_video: motion transfer -> hf_mult_motion_control; object replacement -> hf_mult_replace_object. For top/popular/trending Genjutsu, first get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu-trending; never legacy motion_control or ad-multiplier for one Genjutsu edit. Without an explicit preset recipe, for multi-step videos call get_workflow_instructions first (with no argument). For clip edits call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "ad-multiplier" } first. AI Influencer: ai_influencer_prepare then ai_influencer_generate. Character sheets: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "character-sheet" }; websites/apps/games: call get_workflow_instructions with { workflow: "website-builder-flow" }. Character sheets require explicit requests. Bundled files: get_workflow_bundle_file. For AI Influencer chat creation, use ai_influencer_get_options for explicit traits, ai_influencer_list_presets for examples, or ai_influencer_get_settings with job_id for an existing sheet. ai_influencer_prepare returns design and price without generation. Preserve references and seed; use randomize=false for exact settings. Pass prepared params unchanged to ai_influencer_generate with max_credits at the quote or a lower user budget. Existing creation intent permits proceeding within budget; preview-only requests must stop after preparation. For explicit free-only intent, require known available free_gens_remaining and use_free_gens=true with max_credits=0; never fall back to credits. For variants, prepare each sheet and respect total count and aggregate budget. The generator opens an auto-updating widget for progress and the completed sheet. Wait with jobs_wait (timeout_seconds <= 15); do not duplicate the display with show_generation_by_ids or job_display unless explicitly requested. Offer Genjutsu animation afterward unless declined; require agreement and selection of the exact completed character before get_presets source=genjutsu category=genjutsu with initial_inputs.character_sheet=[{id:job_id,type:image_job}]. Opening that gallery does not authorize video submission. If chat creation is unavailable, report it without silently switching to generic image generation or the builder UI. Multiple independent generations: batch tools, jobs_wait, then one show_generation_by_ids. Use generate_3d to turn an image into a 3D GLB mesh. When unsure which model fits, call models_explore(action:'recommend') before calling a generate_* tool. Use virality_predictor when the user asks to predict video virality or analyze engagement, attention, audience response, retention risk, hook strength, or creative performance. For other existing-asset edits use upscale_image/video, outpaint_image, reframe, remove_background, relight_image, or motion_control (single-character Kling recast). For voice creation in Apps UI-capable clients, call create_voice … [truncated]

## slide-studio
First call list_editors and use the registered local browser tab. Never open or connect CarouselBot through a sandboxed agent browser. If no editor is listed, retry briefly because browser reconnection is automatic, then ask the user to open https://carousel.bot in their normal browser and click Connect AI. Companion compatibility and reconnects are automatic. Do not parallel-retry an action that reports an unsupported internal action; retry once after list_editors so automatic recovery can finish. Never restart a healthy companion for a transient editor disconnect. Before edits call get_design_guidance, then begin_edit_session; pass editSessionId to every edit and end it in cleanup. Parallel workers can share the same browser tab and project; sessions track targets without exclusive locks. Use render_slide to inspect actual pixels.

41	    def __init__(self, kind: str, msg: str = ""):

53	    status: str  # pass | fail | skipped | error
54	    trace_id: str | None = None
55	    agent_model: str | None = None

73	class EvalExecutor(Protocol):
74	    """Runs one case `repeats` times at a checked-out commit. Tests supply a fake; production uses SubprocessExecutor."""

76	    def run_case(self, req: CaseRequest) -> list[RunResult]: ...

79	def parse_report(report: dict) -> list[RunResult]:
80	    if report.get("schema_version") != 1:
81	        raise EvalInfraError("crash", f"unsupported schema_version {report.get('schema_version')!r}")
82	    return [RunResult(case_id=r["case_id"], status=r["status"], trace_id=r.get("trace_id"),

90	def _json_tail(out: str) -> str:
91	    """The JSON report starts at the first line that is exactly '{'; tolerate SDK log lines printed before it."""
92	    i = 0 if out.lstrip().startswith("{") else out.find("\n{\n") + 1

96	class SubprocessExecutor:
97	    def __init__(self, eval_cmd: list[str] | None = None):
98	        self.eval_cmd = eval_cmd or ["uv", "run", "python", "-m", "evals"]

100	    def run_case(self, req: CaseRequest) -> list[RunResult]:
101	        cmd = [*self.eval_cmd, "run", "--json", "--isolate", "--suite", "all", "--cases", req.case,
102	               "--repeats", str(req.repeats), "--commit", req.sha, "--run-id", req.run_id]

138	    env_file: str | None = None  # KEY=VALUE lines (API keys) injected into eval subprocesses; never logged

141	    # Local Anthropic-compatible proxy (agentbisect llm-proxy): sets ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL + a dummy key in eval env.

145	def config_from_env(cases: list[str], **kw) -> RunnerConfig:
146	    """RunnerConfig with operator overrides from the environment (budget control for live runs):
147	    AGENTBISECT_REPEATS, _MAX_REPEATS, _WORKERS, _ENV_FILE, _BASELINE."""
148	    env = os.environ
149	    for key, name, conv in (("repeats", "AGENTBISECT_REPEATS", int), ("max_repeats", "AGENTBISECT_MAX_REPEATS", int), ("judge_repeats", "AGENTBISECT_JUDGE_REPEATS", int),

151	                            ("baseline", "AGENTBISECT_BASELINE", str)):

157	def default_classify(cfg: RunnerConfig) -> Callable[[float, int], str]:
158	    def f(rate: float, n: int) -> str:
159	        return "good" if rate >= cfg.good_min else "bad" if rate <= cfg.bad_max else "uncertain"

163	@contextlib.contextmanager
164	def worktree(repo: Path, sha: str, root: str | None = None) -> Iterator[Path]:
165	    """Detached worktree at sha in a temp dir; always removed and pruned, even on error."""
166	    tmp = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="agentbisect-wt-", dir=root))
167	    path = tmp / "wt"
168	    try:
169	        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "add", "--detach", str(path), sha],
170	                       capture_output=True, text=True, check=True)
171	        yield path
172	    finally:
173	        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "remove", "--force", str(path)], capture_output=True)
174	        shutil.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
175	        subprocess.run(["git", "-C", str(repo), "worktree", "prune"], capture_output=True)

178	def _load_env_file(path: str | None) -> dict[str, str]:
179	    out: dict[str, str] = {}
180	    if path and Path(path).exists():
181	        for line in Path(path).read_text().splitlines():
182	            line = line.strip()
183	            if line and not line.startswith("#") and "=" in line:
184	                k, v = line.split("=", 1)
185	                out[k.strip()] = v.strip().strip("'\"")
186	    return out

189	class Runner:
190	    def __init__(self, repo: str | Path, cfg: RunnerConfig, cache: VerdictCache,
191	                 executor: EvalExecutor | None = None, sleep: Callable[[float], None] = time.sleep,
192	                 signature: FailureSignature | None = None):
193	        self.signature = signature  # when set, pass/fail means "this failing check does not occur"
194	        self.repo = Path(repo).resolve()
195	        self.cfg = cfg
196	        self.cache = cache
197	        self.executor = executor or SubprocessExecutor()
198	        self.sleep = sleep
199	        self.classify = cfg.classify or default_classify(cfg)
200	        self.eval_rounds = 0  # individual eval runs executed (not cache hits): the smart-vs-plain metric
201	        self._lock = threading.Lock()
202	
203	    # -- install --
204	
205	    def _install(self, wt: Path) -> None:
206	        if not self.cfg.install_cmd:
207	            return
208	        try:
209	            p = subprocess.run(self.cfg.install_cmd, cwd=wt, capture_output=True, text=True,
210	                               timeout=self.cfg.install_timeout, env=self._env(None, None, None))
211	        except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
212	            raise BuildError(f"install timed out after {self.cfg.install_timeout}s")
213	        except OSError as e:
214	            raise BuildError(f"install could not start: {e}")
215	        if p.returncode != 0:
216	            raise BuildError(f"install failed (exit {p.returncode}): {(p.stderr or p.stdout)[-300:].strip()}")
217	
218	    def _env(self, sha: str | None, run_id: str | None, case: str | None, salt: str | None = None) -> dict[str, str]:
219	        env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k not in ("VIRTUAL_ENV", "PYTHONPATH")}
220	        env.update(_load_env_file(self.cfg.env_file))
221	        # The neatlogs SDK logs "shutdown complete" to STDOUT at INFO, which corrupts the harness's JSON report.
222	        env.setdefault("NEATLOGS_LOG_LEVEL", "ERROR")
223	        if self.cfg.llm_proxy_url:
224	            # the salt rides in the URL path (not the prompt): the proxy keys its response cache on it, so repeat i of
225	            # a case at a commit is its own sample, and replaying the same (commit, case, repeat) hits the cache
226	            env["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = self.cfg.llm_proxy_url.rstrip("/") + (f"/salt/{salt}" if salt else "")
227	            env["ANTHROPIC_API_KEY"] = "agentbisect-proxy"
228	        for k, v in (("AGENTBISECT_COMMIT", sha), ("AGENTBISECT_RUN_ID", run_id), ("AGENTBISECT_CASE", case)):
229	            if v:
230	                env[k] = v
231	        return env
232	
233	    # -- one case, with retries --
234	
235	    def _run_case(self, wt: Path, sha: str, case: str, n: int, run_id: str, base: int = 0) -> list[RunResult]:
236	        """Run `case` n more times (repeat indices base..). Rate limits and timeouts retry (only the missing runs)
237	        with exponential backoff; runs still failing after max_retries become 'error' results, i.e. no verdict
238	        rather than a bad verdict. Through the LLM proxy every repeat is its own request with its own salt."""
239	        results: list[RunResult] = []
240	        last = "unknown"
241	        for attempt in range(self.cfg.max_retries + 1):
242	            remaining = n - len(results)
243	            for b in ([1] * remaining if self.cfg.llm_proxy_url else [remaining]):
244	                done = sum(r.status in ("pass", "fail") for r in results)
245	                errs = sum(r.status == "error" for r in results)  # an errored run left cached replies: new salt
246	                salt = (f"{sha[:12]}.{hashlib.sha1(case.encode()).hexdigest()[:10]}.r{base + done}"
247	                        + (f".e{errs}" if errs else "")) if self.cfg.llm_proxy_url else None
248	                req = CaseRequest(wt, sha, case, b, run_id, self._env(sha, run_id, case, salt), self.cfg.timeout,
249	                                  self.cfg.baseline)
250	                try:
251	                    got = self.executor.run_case(req)
252	                except EvalInfraError as e:
253	                    last = str(e)
254	                    break
255	                self._check_pins(got)
256	                retry = [r for r in got if r.status == "error" and RATE_LIMIT_RE.search(r.reason)]
257	                results += [r for r in got if r not in retry]
258	                if retry:
259	                    last = f"rate_limit: {retry[0].reason}"
260	                    break  # back off before the next attempt instead of firing the rest back to back
261	            if len(results) >= n:
262	                return results
263	            if attempt < self.cfg.max_retries:
264	                self.sleep(self.cfg.backoff * (2 ** attempt))
265	        return results + [RunResult(case, "error", reason=f"{last} (gave up after {self.cfg.max_retries + 1} attempts)")
266	                          for _ in range(n - len(results))]
267	
268	    def _check_pins(self, results: list[RunResult]) -> None:
269	        for r in results:
270	            if r.status in ("skipped", "error"):
271	                continue
272	            for key in ("agent_model", "judge_model"):
273	                got = getattr(r, key)
274	                if got != self.cfg.models[key]:
275	                    raise ModelPinError(
276	                        f"{r.case_id}: {key} {got!r} != pinned {self.cfg.models[key]!r}; refusing to mix models")
277	
278	    # -- one commit --
279	
280	    def evaluate_commit(self, sha: str, run_id: str, cases: list[str] | None = None) -> CommitResult:
281	        """K cases x R repeats at `sha` in one worktree, `workers` cases in parallel. While the verdict is inside
282	        the confidence band, cases that disagree with themselves (or fail, at one repeat) get doubled repeats up to
283	        max_repeats; judge-graded cases always run `judge_repeats`; if it is
284	        still uncertain the verdict is 'flaky'. Build/worktree failure => 'skip' (cached). Finished cases are
285	        cached immediately, so a crash mid-step loses at most the in-flight cases."""
286	        sig = self.signature
287	        cases = list(cases or (sig.cases if sig and sig.cases else None) or self.cfg.cases)
288	        models = self.cfg.models
289	        cached_skip = self.cache.get(sha, BUILD_CASE, models)
290	        if cached_skip:
291	            return CommitResult("skip", reason=cached_skip["skip"], from_cache=True)
292	
293	        def have(case: str) -> dict:
294	            return self.cache.get(sha, case, models) or {}
295	
296	        def need(case: str, target: int) -> int:
297	            e = have(case)  # executed runs, whatever failed in them
298	            return 0 if "skip" in e else max(0, target - e.get("runs", 0))
299	
300	        errors: dict[str, int] = {c: 0 for c in cases}
301	        wt_ctx = None
302	        wt: Path | None = None
303	        ran = False
304	
305	        def work(cn: tuple[str, int]) -> None:
306	            case, n = cn
307	            base = have(case).get("runs", 0)
308	            results = self._run_case(wt, sha, case, n, run_id, base)
309	            p = sum(r.status == "pass" for r in results)
310	            f = sum(r.status == "fail" for r in results)
311	            errors[case] += sum(r.status == "error" for r in results)
312	            if results and all(r.status == "skipped" for r in results):
313	                self.cache.set_case_skip(sha, case, models, results[0].reason or "skipped by target")
314	                return
315	            with self._lock:
316	                self.eval_rounds += p + f
317	            k = base
318	            for r in results:
319	                if r.status not in ("pass", "fail"):
320	                    continue
321	                recs = r.failures or ([{"key": "case_fail", "check": "case_fail", "reason": r.reason}]
322	                                      if r.status == "fail" else [])  # a failing run always has a cause key
323	                self.cache.add_run(sha, case, models, k, r.status, r.trace_id, {x["key"]: x for x in recs})
324	                k += 1
325	
326	        try:
327	            with step_span("evaluate_commit", sha=sha, run_id=run_id):
328	                active, target = cases, self.cfg.repeats
329	                while True:
330	                    todo = [(c, need(c, max(target, self.cfg.judge_repeats) if c in self.cfg.judge_cases else target))
331	                            for c in active]
332	                    todo = [t for t in todo if t[1] > 0]
333	                    if todo and wt_ctx is None:
334	                        wt_ctx = worktree(self.repo, sha, self.cfg.worktree_root)
335	                        try:
336	                            wt = wt_ctx.__enter__()
337	                            self._install(wt)
338	                        except (BuildError, subprocess.CalledProcessError) as e:
339	                            msg = str(e) if isinstance(e, BuildError) else \
340	                                f"git worktree failed: {(e.stderr or '').strip()[-200:]}"
341	                            self.cache.set_skip(sha, models, msg)
342	                            return CommitResult("skip", reason=msg)
343	                    if todo:
344	                        with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max(1, self.cfg.workers)) as pool:
345	                            list(pool.map(work, todo))
346	                        ran = True
347	                    stats = self._tally(sha, cases, errors)
348	                    passes = sum(t["passes"] for t in stats.values())
349	                    fails = sum(t["fails"] for t in stats.values())
350	                    if passes + fails == 0 and self.signature and not any(errors.values()) and all(
351	                            "skip" in (self.cache.get(sha, c, models) or {}) for c in cases):
352	                        # the signature's cases do not exist at this commit (e.g. they need a tool added later):
353	                        # the failure cannot occur here, so it is vacuously good, not an unusable commit
354	                        return CommitResult("good", pass_rate=1.0, executed=0, case_stats={}, from_cache=not ran,
355	                                            reason="signature cases not applicable at this commit")
356	                    if passes + fails == 0:
357	                        return CommitResult("skip", reason="no executed runs (all errored or skipped)",
358	                                            case_stats=stats)
359	                    rate = passes / (passes + fails)
360	                    band = self.classify(rate, passes + fails)
361	                    # borderline: re-run the cases that disagree with themselves; with a single sample per case there
362	                    # is no disagreement to see yet, so re-run every failing case
363	                    flaky = [c for c, t in stats.items() if t["passes"] and t["fails"]]
364	                    again = flaky or ([c for c, t in stats.items() if t["fails"]] if target <= 1 else [])
365	                    if band != "uncertain" or not again or target >= self.cfg.max_repeats:
366	                        break
367	                    target, active = min(self.cfg.max_repeats, target * 2), again
368	        finally:
369	            if wt_ctx is not None:
370	                wt_ctx.__exit__(None, None, None)
371	
372	        traces = [t for c in stats for t in (have(c).get("trace_ids") or [])]
373	        verdict = {"good": "good", "bad": "bad"}.get(band, "flaky")
374	        return CommitResult(
375	            verdict, pass_rate=rate, trace_ids=traces, executed=passes + fails, repeats=target,
376	            flaky_cases=flaky, failing_cases=[c for c, t in stats.items() if t["fails"] and not t["passes"]],
377	            case_stats=stats, from_cache=not ran,
378	            failure_signatures=self._signatures(sha, cases),
379	            reason=(f"pass_rate {rate:.2f} inside band ({self.cfg.bad_max}, {self.cfg.good_min}) after "
380	                    f"{target} repeats" if verdict == "flaky" else ""))
381	
382	    def _tally(self, sha: str, cases: list[str], errors: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, dict[str, int]]:
383	        """Per case passes/fails/errors. With a signature a run only counts as failed when that check failed in
384	        it; any other failure (another regression's budget miss, say) is a pass for this signature."""
385	        out = {}
386	        for c in cases:
387	            e = self.cache.get(sha, c, self.cfg.models) or {}
388	            if "skip" in e:
389	                continue
390	            runs = e.get("passes", 0) + e.get("fails", 0)
391	            fails = e.get("fails", 0)
392	            if self.signature:
393	                key = self.signature.key  # a bare `budget:tokens` also covers the per-category `budget:tokens@cat`
394	                cf = e.get("check_fails") or {}
395	                fails = min(runs, sum(n for k, n in cf.items() if k == key or k.startswith(key + "@")))
396	            out[c] = {"passes": runs - fails, "fails": fails, "errors": errors.get(c, 0)}
397	        return out
398	
399	    def signatures_at(self, sha: str, cases: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
400	        return self._signatures(sha, cases)
401	
402	    def _signatures(self, sha: str, cases: list[str]) -> list[dict]:
403	        """Every failing check seen at `sha` over `cases`, grouped by key (see signature.py)."""
404	        infos: dict[str, dict] = {}
405	        runs: dict[str, int] = {}
406	        fails: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = {}
407	        for c in cases:
408	            e = self.cache.get(sha, c, self.cfg.models) or {}
409	            if "skip" in e:
410	                continue
411	            runs[c] = e.get("passes", 0) + e.get("fails", 0)
412	            fails[c] = dict(e.get("check_fails") or {})
413	            for k, rec in (e.get("check_info") or {}).items():
414	                infos.setdefault(k, rec)
415	        return group_signatures(infos, runs, fails)

- `agentbisect/report.py`: `build_report(state)` -> one dict rendered by `render_markdown` / `render_html` (self-contained, inline CSS, everything html-escaped; Markdown fences widen past backticks in untrusted text). Sections: culprit, labelled original intent (checkpoint vs "NO CHECKPOINT" commit-message fallback), semantic diff + symbols, trace divergence, revert test, confidence + "multiple regressions likely" warning, smart-vs-plain (from `metrics.comparison`, now saved by `agentbisect compare`), fix section ("not attempted" without a FixAttempt; "NOT verified" draft variant when the best attempt misses baseline-0.1 or the intent test), context tokens per step, commits table, trace ids + links, Entire checkpoint ids (git trailer, best effort) + `entire checkpoint explain <sha> --full`.
- `open_pr(state, repo, draft=None, confirm=False, run=...)`: DRY-RUN by default (prints title/body/`git push` + `gh pr create`); only `--open-pr --confirm-open-pr` executes; body ends with the Claude Code line. Tests inject a stub runner, nothing is pushed. After a confirmed PR the status becomes `reported`.

Each call shells out to `claude -p --model <exact id> --output-format json --tools "" --system-prompt ... --setting-sources "" --strict-mcp-config --no-session-persistence` in an empty temp cwd. Credentials are never read; only the binary is run.
- Tool use is emulated: schemas + conversation (incl. tool_use/tool_result history) rendered into the prompt, `--json-schema` forces `{text, tool_calls[{name,input}]}`; output validated against the supplied input_schemas (retry once with the error, then 502 Anthropic-style error); blocks get `toolu_*` ids, stop_reason tool_use/end_turn. Tool-free requests (judge) pass the single user message straight through, no schema. tool_choice any/tool enforced, none drops tools. The prompt must say outright that tools are available (first attempt made Haiku claim it had no tools).
- Response `model` and tokens come from the requested model's `modelUsage` entry (the side call to another model is ignored for tokens, included in cost). Rate limits (is_error/api_error_status 429/529 or text match) retry with exponential backoff, then HTTP 429 + `retry-after` so SDK retries behave. Semaphore caps concurrency. Optional cache `.agentbisect/llm_cache` keyed by sha256(model, system, messages, tools, tool_choice).
- LIMITS: temperature cannot be set (logged in /stats `temperatures`, otherwise ignored), so runs are not temperature-0 deterministic. Input tokens include ~1.2k of CLI overhead per call plus the emulated tool prompt (~6k per tool turn with the demo's schemas), so token budgets are inflated but consistent; do not compare against raw API counts. ~3-8 s per call.

The verdict cache stores per-check failures, so the runner counts a run as failed only when THIS signature fails (other regressions' failures are passes) and evaluates only the signature's cases. The signature comes from trace hints (`failed_checks` metadata / `check:` tag, none exist on real neatlogs traces yet) or is discovered at the bad end (`_discover_signature`; deterministic check preferred over budget, bad trace's case preferred). Revert test uses the same predicate. `investigate --all-signatures` (default: on when several) spawns one sibling investigation per remaining signature (shared cache), `--signature KEY` forces one. Planner gets signature words + graph-impact hints (tool, refund/amount). Report has a "Failure signature" section stating it separates overlapping regressions by signature. Review fixes: siblings always run, bad-end error names the signature. Known: an explicit/trace-supplied signature skips discovery, so no siblings.
- U3 weighted bisect (`planner.weighted_pick`): probe the commit that splits the cumulative rank-score mass (plus a small floor) in half. Uniform or absent scores reduce to exactly plain bisect (property tested); a budget guard (each probe leaves <= 2^(b-1) positions per side, b = plain's worst case minus probes spent) bounds total probes by ceil(log2 K), i.e. never above plain's WORST case, and within one probe of plain on any single culprit (property tested). """Core data shapes (see the plan's "Key data shapes"). Every class round-trips through plain JSON dicts."""
from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass, field
from typing import Any

STATUSES = ("created", "running", "paused", "failed", "culprit_found", "fixing", "verifying", "reported")
VERDICTS = ("good", "bad", "flaky", "skip")


@dataclass
class FailureSignature:
    """The specific check that fails (not just the case): `key` identifies it across cases and commits, e.g.
    `call_args:issue_refund.amount` with expected 64.0 and got 6400. Bisecting on a signature ignores other
    failures (a budget regression elsewhere) so overlapping regressions can be separated."""
    key: str
    check: str = ""  # call_args | reply_regex | budget | judge | ...
    detail: str = ""  # e.g. issue_refund.amount
    expected: str = ""
    got: str = ""
    reason: str = ""
    cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # cases in which it fails at the bad end
    fails: int = 0  # failing runs at the bad end (when discovered)
    runs: int = 0

    @property
    def label(self) -> str:
        s = f"check={self.check}" + (f"({self.detail})" if self.detail else "")
        if self.expected or self.got:
            s += f" expected {self.expected} got {self.got}"
        return s

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "FailureSignature":
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class RegressionSpec:
    source: str = "trace"  # trace | detection | issue
    bad_trace_id: str | None = None
    good_trace_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    held_out: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    predicate: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)  # {"checks": [...], "rubric": str|None}
    metric: str = "pass_rate"
    bad_case: str | None = None  # the case the bad trace maps to
    signature: FailureSignature | None = None  # the failing check being bisected (None = whole-case pass rate)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "RegressionSpec":
        d = dict(d)
        if d.get("signature"):
            d["signature"] = FailureSignature.from_dict(d["signature"])
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class Candidate:
    sha: str
    score: float = 0.0
    reason: str = ""


@dataclass
class Plan:
    divergent_span: str | None = None
    impacted_symbols: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    candidates: list[Candidate] = field(default_factory=list)
    mode: str = "smart"  # smart | plain

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "Plan":
        d = dict(d)
        d["candidates"] = [Candidate(**c) for c in d.get("candidates", [])]
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class CommitResult:
    """Verdict for one commit: results{sha: verdict, pass_rate, trace_ids} plus flaky/skip detail."""
    verdict: str  # good | bad | flaky | skip
    pass_rate: float | None = None
    trace_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    reason: str = ""  # why skipped / flaky
    executed: int = 0
    repeats: int = 0  # repeats per case actually used (after escalation)
    flaky_cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    failing_cases: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    case_stats: dict[str, dict[str, int]] = field(default_factory=dict)  # case -> passes/fails/errors
    failure_signatures: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)  # every failing check seen, grouped
    from_cache: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "CommitResult":
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class BisectState:
    id: str
    repo: str = ""
    good_sha: str | None = None
    bad_sha: str | None = None
    spec: RegressionSpec | None = None
    plan: Plan | None = None
    results: dict[str, CommitResult] = field(default_factory=dict)
    step: int = 0
    status: str = "created"
    in_flight: dict[str, Any] | None = None  # step started but not completed (set => crashed mid-step)
    context_tokens_per_step: list[dict[str, Any]] = field(default_factory=list)  # {step, label, tokens}
    pinned_models: dict[str, str] = field(default_factory=dict)
    culprit: "CulpritReport | None" = None
    fix_attempts: list["FixAttempt"] = field(default_factory=list)
    created_at: str = ""
    updated_at: str = ""
    error: str | None = None
    # engine bookkeeping: strategy, eval_rounds, cost_usd, cache_hits, warnings[], confidence_band, ambiguous[]
    metrics: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return {
            **{k: v for k, v in asdict(self).items()
               if k not in ("spec", "plan", "results", "culprit", "fix_attempts")},
            "spec": self.spec.to_dict() if self.spec else None,
            "plan": self.plan.to_dict() if self.plan else None,
            "results": {s: r.to_dict() for s, r in self.results.items()},
            "culprit": self.culprit.to_dict() if self.culprit else None,
            "fix_attempts": [f.to_dict() for f in self.fix_attempts],
        }

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "BisectState":
        d = dict(d)
        d["spec"] = RegressionSpec.from_dict(d["spec"]) if d.get("spec") else None
        d["plan"] = Plan.from_dict(d["plan"]) if d.get("plan") else None
        d["results"] = {s: CommitResult.from_dict(r) for s, r in d.get("results", {}).items()}
        d["culprit"] = CulpritReport.from_dict(d["culprit"]) if d.get("culprit") else None
        d["fix_attempts"] = [FixAttempt.from_dict(f) for f in d.get("fix_attempts", [])]
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class CulpritReport:
    sha: str
    checkpoint_intent: str = ""
    semantic_diff: str = ""
    impacted_symbols: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    revert_test_passed: bool | None = None  # None = not run / inconclusive
    confidence: str = ""  # e.g. high | medium | low
    # chunk 8 additions (all optional so older saved states still load)
    intent_source: str = ""  # checkpoint | commit_message
    trace_divergence: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # span-by-span good-vs-bad summary
    failing_evidence: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # what the Fixer is shown about the failure
    flags: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)  # e.g. "multiple regressions likely", "revert conflicts"
    revert_details: dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
    analyzed: bool = False

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "CulpritReport":
        return cls(**d)


@dataclass
class FixAttempt:
    branch: str
    diff: str = ""
    eval_score: float | None = None
    held_out_score: float | None = None
    intent_test_passed: bool | None = None
    trace_ids: list[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    attempt: int = 1

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, Any]:
        return asdict(self)

    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, d: dict[str, Any]) -> "FixAttempt":
        return cls(**d)

def load_cases(repo: str | Path) -> list[Case]:
    p = Path(repo) / "evals" / "cases.jsonl"
    if not p.exists():
        raise IntakeError(f"{p} not found: target repo has no eval cases")
    out = []
    for line in p.read_text().splitlines():
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        d = json.loads(line)
        out.append(Case(id=d["id"], category=d["category"], input=d["input"], checks=d.get("checks", {}),
                        held_out=bool(d.get("held_out")), requires_tool=d.get("requires_tool"),
                        rubric=d.get("rubric")))  # FORBIDDEN_CASE_KEYS are simply never copied
    return out


def build_predicate(cases: list[Case]) -> dict[str, Any]:
    """Deterministic checks first (per case), judge rubric second (only where a case has one), then the budget."""
    return {
        "order": ["checks", "budget", "rubric"],
        "checks": [{"case_id": c.id, "checks": c.checks} for c in cases],
        "budget": dict(BUDGET),
        "rubric": {c.id: c.rubric for c in cases if c.rubric} or None,
    }


def split_suite(cases: list[Case], category_ids: list[str] | set[str] | None) -> tuple[list[Case], list[Case]]:
    """Working suite = non-held-out cases of the given categories (None = every category); held-out = every

    cats = None if category_ids is None else set(category_ids)

7	BUDGET RULE (used by the runner, the bisect and the revert test):
8	  * a budget signature (`budget:tokens...` / `budget:steps...`) runs every one of its cases `budget_repeats` times
9	    (AGENTBISECT_BUDGET_REPEATS, default 3) per commit; behavioural signatures stay at `repeats` (default 1);
10	  * per case, the commit's metric is the MEDIAN over those repeats; the case is over budget when that median
11	    exceeds the limit (tokens: `token_factor` x the case's baseline median; steps: `max_steps`);

I'm adding baseline calibration logic for U2: a helper to compare SHA prefixes for matching commits, a validation method that raises an error if the good SHA or agent model doesn't match, a loader that validates before returning cached data, and a builder function that assembles baseline results across cache entries using the given models, repeats, token factor, and step limits.

Now I'm working out where calibration logic should live to avoid circular imports between the runner and baseline modules, deciding to duck-type the runner object inside baseline.py. The calibrate function temporarily swaps the runner's config to run uncapped budget repeats on the good commit, then filters the cached results to keep only clean pass/fail entries that aren't budget-related and have valid token counts.

I'm computing median tokens and steps per case, excluding cases where nothing ran cleanly or where the target skipped the run, with explanatory notes for each exclusion. I also need to handle cases where the cache already has partial repeat data and just needs topping up to the full repeat count, then format the final baseline with today's date and an ISO timestamp.

Now I'm adding validation logic: checking the baseline has a good_sha, that it was created by calibrate, that the commit and model match expectations, and that cases aren't empty, raising clear errors otherwise. I also need make_runner to load and validate the baseline against the resolved good commit, falling back gracefully if resolution fails, and make sure BaselineError gets caught alongside the other exceptions in run_investigation so failures are reported properly.

I'm also deciding Runner should refuse to evaluate commits needing a budget signature when no baseline exists, raising BaselineError with instructions to run calibrate and set AGENTBISECT_BASELINE — this check needs to happen both in the runner's evaluate_commit method and after signature discovery in run_investigation. But I realize this could break existing tests that construct a Runner directly with a budget signature and no baseline, since those currently work for step-count-style signatures that don't actually need token baselines — so the refusal should probably only apply when the signature truly requires a baseline for comparison.

Thinking through the flow: siblings spawned after a failed primary signature would still run independently, and only the ones that are budget-type would hit the same baseline error, while non-budget siblings continue normally — so a mixed investigation can partially fail without blocking everything else.

Now I'm designing the `calibrate` subcommand: it takes `--repo`, `--good`, `--out`, `--cases`, and `--llm-proxy`, builds a runner config with no baseline set, runs the cases, and prints a summary plus the output path. I'm wiring it into the `_main` dispatch alongside `investigate`, deciding the default output path should live under the state directory as `baseline-<sha8>.json`, and resolving the good commit via `bisect.resolve`.

"""Calibration (`agentbisect calibrate`), baseline validation and the refusal to run budget signatures without one."""

def data(**kw):

def test_validate_accepts_matching_sha_and_model_and_short_sha():

    assert Baseline(data(good_sha=GOOD[:12])).validate(GOOD, PINS["agent_model"])  # prefix either way round


@pytest.mark.parametrize("d, good, model, word", [
    (data(good_sha="b" * 40), GOOD, PINS["agent_model"], "calibrated at bbbbbbbbbb"),

    ({k: v for k, v in data().items() if k != "good_sha"}, GOOD, PINS["agent_model"], "no good_sha"),
    (data(cases={}), GOOD, PINS["agent_model"], "no per-case"),
    (data(good_sha="abc"), "abc", PINS["agent_model"], "calibrated at"),  # too short to trust a prefix match
])

        Baseline.load(tmp_path / "bad.json")

                    {"status": "fail", "tokens": 9999, "steps": 9, "fails": ["call_args:t.x"]},  # wrong behaviour
                    {"status": "pass", "tokens": 110, "steps": 2, "fails": []}]}
    out = build_baseline({"a": e, "b": {"detail": [{"status": "fail", "tokens": 5, "fails": ["judge"]}]}}, GOOD, PINS, 3,
                         {"c": "skipped by the target: no tool"})
    assert out["cases"]["a"] == {"median_tokens": 110, "median_steps": 2, "n": 3}
    assert set(out["excluded_cases"]) == {"b", "c"} and "b" not in out["cases"]
    assert (out["good_sha"], out["commit"], out["agent_model"], out["repeats"]) == (GOOD, GOOD, PINS["agent_model"], 3)
    assert out["date"] and out["created_at"] and out["token_factor"] == 1.5


def test_calibrate_runs_good_commit_three_repeats_without_baseline_and_writes_json(tmp_path, hist):

def test_investigation_refuses_budget_signature_without_baseline_and_never_calibrates(tmp_path, hist, monkeypatch):

    assert ex.reqs == [] and not list((tmp_path / "ab").glob("baseline*"))  # nothing run, nothing calibrated

    ex = Exec(lambda *a: 100)

                    ex, sleep=lambda s: None, signature=st.spec.signature)
    assert B.run_investigation(store, st, runner).kind != "failed" or ex.reqs  # it ran; no baseline error
    assert "calibrate" not in (store.load(st.id).error or "")

    store, st, shas = _inv(tmp_path, hist, TOK)
    f = tmp_path / "base.json"
    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTBISECT_BASELINE", str(f))
    f.write_text(json.dumps(data(good_sha=shas[3])))
    with pytest.raises(BaselineError, match="calibrated at"):
        B.make_runner(store, st)
    f.write_text(json.dumps(data(good_sha=shas[0], agent_model="claude-opus-5")))
    with pytest.raises(BaselineError, match="agent model"):
        B.make_runner(store, st)
    f.write_text(json.dumps(data(good_sha=shas[0])))
    assert B.make_runner(store, st).baseline is not None


def test_mismatched_baseline_fails_the_investigation_with_a_clear_error(tmp_path, hist, monkeypatch):
    store, st, shas = _inv(tmp_path, hist, TOK)
    f = tmp_path / "base.json"
    f.write_text(json.dumps(data(good_sha=shas[5])))
    monkeypatch.setenv("AGENTBISECT_BASELINE", str(f))
    monkeypatch.setattr(R.SubprocessExecutor, "run_case", lambda self, req: pytest.fail("must not evaluate"))
    out = B.run_investigation(store, st)
    assert out.kind == "failed" and "calibrated at" in out.message
